verdict.rationale: Dynadot documents a dedicated API Sandbox on its own host with separate sandbox keys and a pre-funded test balance, so integrations, including registrations, can be tested without real money. The vendor notes that some commands are unavailable or behave differently in the sandbox, and nothing explicitly documents how a developer gets API credentials self-serve. missing for 10: documented self-serve API credential/key provisioning flow, full command parity in the sandbox, independent or hands-on corroboration of sandbox registrations.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get API credentials self-serve and test safely — a sandbox or test environment where registrations don't cost real money

citations.quote: The Dynadot API Sandbox environment allows you to safely test your API integrations without affecting your live account or real funds
pre-funded with a balance of 10,000 in all supported currencies for testing purposes
Build your account by registering, transferring, and renewing domains through commands.
